title: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
subtitle: Calculus · Integral and derivative
summary: Bridges differentiation and integration: the definite integral equals net change in the antiderivative.
detail:
\[ \int_a^b f(x)\,dx = F(b) - F(a) \]

If \(F'=f\) on \([a,b]\), the definite integral equals the net change in \(F\). Part 1: \(\frac{d}{dx}\int_a^x f(t)\,dt = f(x)\) (differentiation undoes integration). Part 2 (shown above): integration computes net change via any antiderivative.
